h1:
Uttaradit–Sukhothai in 3 Days, 2 Nights
Old Towns & Temple Trail
intro: These two provinces sit just 80–90 km apart — an hour and a half of driving — but the stories tucked away here stretch back a thousand years. Sukhothai is the old capital that's now a UNESCO World Heritage Site, while Uttaradit holds the ancient town of Thung Yang and the legendary town of Laplae, which most travellers haven't fully explored. We've laid out a 3-day, 2-night route so you can wander the old cities and visit temples at the same time, with no rush.

blocks.html: The Uttaradit–Sukhothai route suits anyone who loves old towns and easygoing temple trips — no jungle treks or mountain climbs needed. The highlight here is pairing Sukhothai's two World Heritage parks (Sukhothai Historical Park and Si Satchanalai) with Uttaradit's ancient town of Thung Yang and the town of Laplae, all of which happen to sit along the same line. Driving yourself is the smoothest option, but if you don't have a car there are coaches and rental cars in town.

Uttaradit and Sukhothai are linked by Highway 102, with around 80–90 km from town centre to town centre and roughly 1 hour 30 minutes of driving. The road passes right through Si Satchanalai district, so it's easy to stop there before heading into Sukhothai's old city. If you fly into Sukhothai Airport (Bangkok Airways flies direct from Suvarnabhumi in about 1 hour 20 minutes) and rent a car from there, that's the fastest way.

items: Self-drive — the most convenient choice for this trip, since the sights are spread out beyond the towns. Both Si Satchanalai and Thung Yang sit right by the highway, with easy parking.
Coach/van — buses run between Uttaradit and Sukhothai daily, but once you arrive you'll need to catch another ride around town. Best if you're only visiting the old cities.
Bicycle/tram hire — inside both historical parks you can cycle or ride the electric tram to look around. It's a nice way to do it and easy on the site.

blocks.title: Recommended direction
blocks.html: If you're starting from Uttaradit, head down to Sukhothai and Si Satchanalai first, then loop back to finish at Thung Yang and Laplae on the Uttaradit side — that way you won't double back.

blocks.text: Day 1 — Sukhothai Old City, the World Heritage Heart of the Trip

blocks.html: Give the first day fully to Sukhothai Historical Park. Leave Uttaradit town in the morning and the hour-and-a-half drive gets you to Sukhothai's old city just before the sun gets harsh. The park is open 06:30–19:30, with a 20 THB entry fee per zone for Thai visitors, or a combined ticket for 40 THB. Inside the old walls you can cycle around comfortably — hire a bike for a few dozen baht near the park entrance.

items.activity: Leave Uttaradit town and take Highway 102 toward Sukhothai
items.note: Around 80–90 km, roughly 1 hr 30 min. You can stop at a petrol station along the way.

items.activity: Arrive at Sukhothai's old city, hire a bike at the park entrance, buy a ticket for the inner zone
items.note: Combined Thai ticket 40 THB; bike hire around 30–40 THB/day.

items.activity: Wat Mahathat in the centre of the old city, with its lotus-bud chedi and large Buddha image
items.note: The royal temple of the kingdom and the main photo spot in Sukhothai.

items.activity: Wat Sa Si, set in the middle of a pond — the reflection of the chedi is beautiful
items.note: An easy walk or ride on from Wat Mahathat.

items.activity: Break for lunch — try Sukhothai noodles at a spot in the new town
items.note: Sukhothai noodles lean sweet, with yard-long beans and red pork — a local specialty.

items.activity: Wat Si Chum to see Phra Achana, the large Buddha image in a narrow mondop
items.note: Outside the city walls to the northwest, open 07:30–17:00.

items.activity: Head back inside the city walls to catch the evening light at Wat Mahathat
items.note: The light around sunset is soft and lovely, with fewer people — better for photos than midday.

items.activity: Check in near Sukhothai's old town or new town
items.note: The old-town area has guesthouses with nice atmosphere; the new town has more restaurants.

blocks.title: Day 1 tip
blocks.html: Sukhothai's midday sun is strong — bring a hat and water, start early, and save photos for the evening to make it much more comfortable.

blocks.text: Day 2 — Si Satchanalai, the Old Town by the Yom River

blocks.html: On day two, move north toward Si Satchanalai, which happens to be right on the way back to Uttaradit. This ancient town sits beside the Yom River, ringed by hills, with a shadier feel and fewer people than Sukhothai. It's open 08:00–17:00, with a 10 THB entry fee for Thai visitors. The site is set up as a low-carbon zone, so you can walk, cycle or ride the electric tram around it.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Sukhothai → Si Satchanalai Historical Park → into Uttaradit

items.activity: Check out and take Highway 101 toward Si Satchanalai
items.note: About 60 km from Sukhothai's old city, roughly 1 hr.

items.activity: Arrive at Si Satchanalai, buy a ticket, hire a bike or take the tram
items.note: A big site — cycling is a nice way to see it, with plenty of shade.

items.activity: Wat Chang Lom, with around 39 stucco elephants encircling the base of a Lankan-style chedi
items.note: The signature image of Si Satchanalai, with the large main chedi at the centre of town.

items.activity: Wat Chedi Chet Thaeo, with a cluster of more than 30 chedis in varied styles
items.note: In front of Wat Chang Lom, about 150 m on — the royal cemetery in the centre of town.

items.activity: Break for lunch at a local spot around Si Satchanalai district
items.note: There are made-to-order restaurants and roadside noodle stalls at local prices.

items.activity: Stop by the Sukhothai ceramics centre / Thuriang kilns to see where Sangkhalok ware was made
items.note: Small Sangkhalok ceramic pieces make nice souvenirs to take home.

items.activity: Drive back toward Uttaradit town
items.note: Around 60–70 km, roughly 1 hr 15 min.

items.activity: Check in to your hotel in Uttaradit town and rest
items.note: If it's a Saturday, you can stop by the Uttaradit walking street, open 15:00–21:00.

blocks.title: Saturdays have an edge
blocks.html: The Uttaradit walking street runs every Saturday from 15:00–21:00. If you plan the trip so night two lands on a Saturday, you'll get to wander, eat local food and pick up souvenirs at just the right time.

blocks.text: Day 3 — Thung Yang, Laplae Town, and Temples to Close the Trip

blocks.html: Save the last day for the Uttaradit side, the highlight for old-town lovers and temple-goers. Start at the ancient town of Thung Yang in Laplae district, which dates back to the late Sukhothai era, then carry on into the town of Laplae — the legendary place where you mustn't tell a lie. Close out with visits to key temples and a climb up to temples on the hillside.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At → Thung Yang → Laplae town → Phraya Phichai Dap Hak Monument

items.activity: Wat Phra Thaen Sila At, a royal monastery on Khao Tao hill in Thung Yang sub-district
items.note: An old temple central to the town, with the legend of the stone slab where the Buddha is said to have rested.

items.activity: Wat Phra Yuen Phutthabat Yukhon, on the same hill but a different peak — walkable from here
items.note: Visit two temples in one go; the two sit right next to each other.

items.activity: Wat Phra Borommathat Thung Yang, to see the old reliquary chedi and a Lanna-style viharn
items.note: Thought to date to the reign of Phraya Lithai; it enshrines Luang Pho Lak Mueang.

items.activity: Head into Laplae town and stop at the monument to Chao Fa Ham Kuman, the first king of Nakhon Laplae
items.note: In Ban Thong Thap Lae, Fai Luang sub-district — deeply revered by the people of Laplae.

items.activity: Lunch in Laplae town — try the local khao pan phak and mi pan
items.note: Laplae food made by local hands; khao pan phak is the signature local dish.

items.activity: Walk through the Laplae town museum and the Laplae town gateway arch
items.note: Soak up the town's legends and the way of life in Laplae before heading back.

items.activity: Phraya Phichai Dap Hak Monument in front of the provincial hall — close the trip by paying respect to the town's hero
items.note: A landmark check-in spot for Uttaradit, deeply respected by locals.

items.activity: Pick up souvenirs — Long and Lin Laplae durians (in season) or dried goods before the drive home
items.note: Laplae durians appear around June–July; out of season there are processed souvenirs instead.

blocks.text: Adjusting the Plan to the Time You Have

items.name: Only 2 days, 1 night
items.blurb: Combine Sukhothai's old city (day one) with Thung Yang and Laplae (day two), and skip Si Satchanalai for now — save it for a return trip.

items.name: Have a car and time
items.blurb: Add Mae Phun Waterfall in Laplae on the last afternoon, or carry on to Sirikit Dam if you want some natural scenery.

items.name: All about the temples
items.blurb: Focus on temples — trim the parks down to just Wat Mahathat, then pour your time into the key temples in both provinces.

blocks.text: A Few Honest Things to Know Before You Go

items: Strong sun — both Sukhothai and Si Satchanalai are open sites with little shade at midday. Skip noon and go in the morning or evening for more comfort.
Spread-out sights — Thung Yang, Laplae and the two parks sit in different directions, so without your own car you'll lose a fair bit of time changing vehicles.
Laplae durians are seasonal — the famous Long and Lin Laplae varieties only come out around June–July. Come in the wrong season and you won't find fresh fruit.
Shops close early — many local restaurants in Laplae and Si Satchanalai close in the afternoon, so plan lunch for no later than 2 pm.

faq.q: How far is Uttaradit from Sukhothai, and how long does it take?
faq.a: It's about 80–90 km from town centre to town centre — roughly 1 hour 30 minutes driving along Highway 102. The road passes right through Si Satchanalai district, so it's easy to stop and explore on the way.

faq.q: Can you do this trip without your own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's less convenient, since the sights are spread out beyond the towns. Coaches and vans run between Uttaradit and Sukhothai daily, and inside both historical parks you can hire a bike or ride the tram. It's manageable if you only visit the old cities, but if you want to add Thung Yang and Laplae you'll really want a car.

faq.q: How much is entry to Sukhothai and Si Satchanalai Historical Parks?
faq.a: Sukhothai is 20 THB per zone for Thai visitors, or 40 THB for a combined ticket, open 06:30–19:30. Si Satchanalai is 10 THB for Thai visitors, open 08:00–17:00. Bike hire adds around 30–40 THB.

faq.q: What's the best season to go?
faq.a: Late in the year through early next year (November–February) brings cool, comfortable weather and the most enjoyable old-town visits. If you also want Long and Lin Laplae durians you'll need to come in June–July. The rainy season has less harsh sun and lovely greenery.

It suits people who love old towns, history and easygoing temple visits — no jungle treks or mountain climbs. It's easy to get around and works for all ages, including bringing older relatives along without wearing them out.
